messages:
incident-bot: ALERT • p99 latency breached for service=generator-prod (p99=3.4s, threshold=2.0s). Trigger: realtime-p95-p99 detector.
Alex M.: pinging oncall — @Sam O. are you online?
Sam O.: here, just saw the page. landing in 2. on my way. quick question — is this global or region-specific?
Priya S.: looks like eu-west-1 and us-west-2 both spiking. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/apps/latency?svc=generator-prod (watch p95/p99 heatmap).
Marco R.: fyi we got increased 504s reported from a customer in EU20 ~10m ago. logs show streaming stalls (client ACKs paused).
Sam O.: starting quick checks: 1) check autoscaler 2) check model host CPU/GPU 3) verify fallback routing rules.
Jen L.: running tail on runtime: ```kubectl -n rwd logs -l app=generator-prod -c runtime --since=10m | grep -E "stall|kvcache|OOM|error" | tail -n 200```
Jen L.: initial grep: lots of `tail-emit` stalls and `kv-cache-miss` spikes, not OOM. example: `runtime: stall detected seq=512 duration=1.8s host=gpu-32a`
Priya S.: looking at request distribution — median seq length up ~2.1x due to a batch of long-context eval jobs from internal QA. correlates with p95 spike.
Alex M.: is the internal QA traffic pinned to hosted or dedicated? we should throttle if internal.
Marco R.: those eval jobs came from a known CI token (ci-qa). I can mute that token at the ingress if needed.
Sam O.: please mute the CI token now. Marco, can you also push a temporary route to fallback small-model (gpt-small-8k-quant) for non-enterprise customers?
Marco R.: muting token now: `authctl revoke-token ci-qa --env=prod` — done.
Marco R.: routing change: creating canary rule to route 20% of non-prem traffic to gpt-small-8k-quant: ```rwd route create --svc generator-prod --rule "if tier!=enterprise then model=gpt-small-8k-quant percent=20"``` applying...done.
Sam O.: scaling check: autoscaler shows desired replicas increased but some queues backlog due to long decode times. I'll bump max replicas + temporary burst pool.
Jen L.: added burst pool: `infractl scale --pool=burst-gen --replicas=10` — new hosts spinning up, expecting readiness in ~90s.
Priya S.: dashboards: p99 started falling from 3.4s -> 2.6s after token revoke + routing. p95 trending down as well.
Alex M.: customer-impact note for postmortem: one enterprise customer saw intermittent streaming stalls, but no data loss. Marco, can you confirm affected request IDs and user-facing errors?
Marco R.: grabbing request IDs from logs, will post subset. sample reqs: `req_8e3f`, `req_8e40`, `req_8e41` — errors: `stream_timeout` followed by `client_disconnected`.
Sam O.: mitigation checklist: 1) muted noisy CI token 2) canary fallback for smaller model 3) scaled burst pool 4) created alert suppression for noise. Anything else?
Priya S.: we should also enable prefix KV-cache warmup for long-context hot paths — quick patch: set `kv_cache_preload=true` for generator-prod runtime nodes. I can roll that as a config flip.
Jen L.: patch rolling now: `rwd config set generator-prod kv_cache_preload=true --target=burst-gen --rolling 30s`
Sam O.: on-call handoff: I'm going to stay on this for the next 30m. @Alex M. if things look stable at +30, can you take over?
Alex M.: yep, I'll take the 30+ watch. please leave a summary in thread before you hand off.
Priya S.: quick sanity checks list I ran: 
- grafana p95/p99 panels (pattern matched long-seq buckets)
- kernel NVidia GPU metrics: no thermal/driver errors
- ingress latency: no sudden network hops
- model CFG: top-k changed? no.
All point to workload shape change (long inputs) + cache misses.
Marco R.: posting log snippet for context: ```[2026-03-14T10:12:07Z] host=gpu-32a seq=4096 event=kv-cache-miss stall_ms=1840 req=req_8e3f```
Sam O.: status update +25m: p99 ~1.9s, p95 ~0.6s, error rate down. burst hosts healthy, canary routing absorbing some load.
Jen L.: follow-up: I opened a short-term playbook entry for `streaming-stall` with the exact commands we used (revoke internal tokens, route fallback, scale burst pool, toggle kv_cache_preload). link: https://confluence.redwood/ops/playbooks/streaming-stall
Alex M.: thanks team. action items: 
- Marco: collect full list of affected req ids and notify support for customer outreach (ETA 1h)
- Priya: run a short eval to simulate long-context load and verify kv_preload effectiveness (ETA 2h)
- Jen: convert quick commands into runbook steps for oncall (ETA 3h)
- Sam: monitoring: add a short-lived panel to show seq-length distribution vs p99 (ETA 1h)
Marco R.: acknowledged. I'll also check whether CI token allows range queries that cause long sequences and patch.
Sam O.: leaving handoff note: will mark RESOLVED if metrics stay stable for next 15m.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • status=investigating -> mitigated. p99 back within SLO.
Alex M.: closing loop: metrics looked stable for 40m. prepping incident summary and severity assessment for triage meeting.
Jen L.: adding customer impact note to thread: affected customer saw degraded streaming quality for ~12 minutes. no data corruption.
Priya S.: postmortem draft will include root cause hypothesis: internal long-context evals + cold KV-cache causing tail decode stalls, and remediation plan (token hygiene, kv_preload, alert tuning).
Sam O.: final note: thanks everyone. good quick coordination. :thumbsup:
